types.name: IDerivedDataRemoteBackend
types.doc:
A remote tier of the cache that is not a mounted folder: the HTTP backend in
the Http module (Filesystem sits below Http and cannot link curl), or a test
double. Every call is blocking and may run on any loader thread, so an
implementation is thread-safe and never throws; a failure is a miss.

members.signature: virtual bool Put(const std::string& key, const void* data, size_t size) = 0
members.doc:
May return before the bytes have left the machine; a Put that the
remote later rejects costs a future miss, never a wrong hit.

types.name: FDerivedDataCache
types.doc:
Hash-keyed store for build artifacts derived from source assets (decoded
textures, cooked meshes, compiled materials, transpiled graphs). The key
encodes everything affecting the output — source-content hash + import-
settings fingerprint + producer version — so a stale entry can never be
returned; it simply has a different key. Backed by the project's
DerivedDataCache/ directory (gitignored, shareable across machines).

members.name: SetBundledRoot
members.doc:
Read-only fallback root shipped with a packaged game
(<GameRoot>/Content/Paks/DerivedDataCache — baked reflection probes).
Reads probe the writable root first, then this one; writes always go
to the writable root. Survives Initialize; empty clears it.

members.name: SetSharedRoot
members.signature: void SetSharedRoot(const std::filesystem::path& sharedRoot, bool writable)
members.doc:
Team-shared cache tier (a network mount / synced folder). Read
order becomes local → shared → bundled; a shared hit is copied
into the local root so the next read never crosses the network.
When `writable`, every Put also lands in the shared root (atomic
temp+rename, so concurrent writers of the same key are safe — the
key encodes the content, either winner is correct). Initialize
picks the MOWO_SHARED_DDC environment variable up automatically
(MOWO_SHARED_DDC_READONLY=1 keeps it read-only); this setter is
for tests and tooling. Empty clears the tier.

members.name: SetRemoteBackend
members.doc:
Remote tier, read after the shared folder and before the bundled root.
A remote hit is written into the local root, and with a writable remote
every Put is also sent there. Initialize picks MOWO_DDC_HTTP (base URL,
the protocol is GET/PUT <base>/ddc/v1/<key>), MOWO_DDC_HTTP_TOKEN (sent
as a bearer token) and MOWO_DDC_HTTP_READONLY=1 up from the
environment. Null clears the tier.

members.signature: using FRemoteBackendFactory = std::shared_ptr<IDerivedDataRemoteBackend> (*)(const std::string& url, const std::string& token, bool writable)
members.doc:
The HTTP tier needs curl, which lives in the Http module above this one.
Http registers the factory when it loads; a URL set before that is kept
and applied on registration. An empty URL clears the tier.

members.name: BuildScope
members.doc:
What the key folds in beyond its four arguments: the engine version, the
platform token and the cache's own format revision. Neither of the first
two used to be there, so a shared tier mounted by a Windows and a macOS
machine filed a BC7 blob and an ASTC blob of the same texture under one
name, and whichever wrote last was handed to both. The git commit is
deliberately NOT in it: every commit would throw the whole cache away,
and a code change that alters a producer's bytes is exactly what that
producer's version argument exists to say. Exposed so a test can read
what it is keying on.

members.name: Purge
members.doc:
Delete every entry in the writable root; returns the bytes freed. The
shared tier belongs to the team and the bundled tier ships inside the
game, so neither is ever touched.

members.name: EvictToBudget
members.doc:
Delete least-recently-used entries until the writable root fits in
`maxBytes`; returns the bytes freed, 0 when it already fits. A producer
version bump orphans every entry it wrote rather than replacing them —
the key changes — so without this the cache only ever grows. An entry's
stamp is its last write or its last hit, refreshed at most once per
AccessStampGranularity so a hot read is not a write every time.

members.name: SetMaxSizeBytes
members.doc:
Size cap enforced after each Put. 0 disables the cap. Seeded from the
`ddc.MaxSizeMB` cvar at Initialize.

members.name: Contains
members.doc:
A zero-length entry is never a hit: every one on disk is a write that
died between create and data, and answering with it pinned a key to
"cached, and empty" forever. Put refuses an empty payload for the same
reason.

types.name: FEmbeddedCryptoKeys
types.doc:
The content keys a packaged game host carries. A game host executable
reserves one block (MOWO_IMPLEMENT_EMBEDDED_CRYPTO_KEYS) that the build leaves
unpatched; `mbt package` finds it in the STAGED copy of the host and writes the
project's encryption key and signing public key into it, so the keys never
sit in a file inside the package and the shared build tree never carries a
project's keys. The host registers the block into FMeafKeyRing before the
first archive mounts.

Each key is split into two random shares XORed with a position mask; neither
share, nor the block searched for a 32-byte run, is the key. That is
obfuscation against a casual scan, not secrecy — the key is in the binary by
construction, as in every engine that ships encrypted paks.

Layout (BlockSize bytes): [0,16) marker, [16,20) "KEYS" once patched,
[20] HasEncryption|HasSigning, [24,28) encryption key id (little endian),
[32,64)+[64,96) encryption key shares, [96,128)+[128,160) signing public key
shares. MBT's EmbeddedCryptoBlock writes the same layout.

members.name: Mask
members.doc: The mask of key byte `index` (0-31 encryption, 32-63 signing).

types.name: FEmbeddedFileSystem
types.doc:
Files a module linked into its own binary (MBT's embedded content: the
module's Content/ folder, read through Core/ModuleContent.h), served as a
read-only file system. The VFS mounts every registered set below every other
mount, so a loose file on disk or an entry in a mounted .meaf answers first
and the embedded copy is only what is left when nothing else has the file.
That is how the editor, the project launcher and the crash reporter find
their fonts, icons and themes with no EngineContent.meaf beside them.

types.name: FModuleSignature
types.doc:
Detached EdDSA signatures for loadable modules. `mbt package` signs every
shipped module binary into "<path>.mowosig" with the project's signing key;
a host that carries the matching PUBLIC key installs VerifyForLoad as the
FModuleManager verify-before-load gate, so a module whose bytes are unsigned
or altered is refused BEFORE its image is ever mapped (and before its
DllMain runs).

One trust root: the key FMeafKeyRing::SetSigningPublicKey registered, the
same key the content archives verify against. It is never read from the
sidecar — a sidecar carries only the 64-byte signature, so an attacker
cannot re-sign a tampered module with a key of their own. No module is
exempt by name: engine modules are signed like plugins, and a DLL named
"MowoEngine.X" proves nothing.

archive entry says yes — reopening it throws away a decompressed

a handle held across calls pins the file against rename and delete
on Windows, which the editor does to loose assets.

members.doc:
Signers this archive may carry instead of the ring key, set before Load.
A mod is signed by its author, not by the game, and the ring check
refused every such pak; with a list set, the embedded key must be one
of these and the signature is checked against it.

members.name: GetSignerKey
members.doc: The key the archive's signature verified against. False when unsigned.

members.name: GetDictionaryCount

members.name: ShouldVerifyOnRead
members.doc:
Payload verification (`meaf.Verify`, see MEAFFileSystem.cpp):
0 = off, 1 = per-entry CRC32 when a whole entry loads (default),
2 = also check the data section against the signature.
Level 2 is the only check that makes a SIGNATURE mean anything about
the payload — the signature covers header+TOC+dataHash, and nothing
used to compare the data section against that hash. It is therefore
the default for a signed archive. A v7 archive pays for it per 64 KiB
block on the first read that touches the block; an older one hashes
the whole data section at mount.

members.name: VerifyDataSectionHash
members.doc:

(v7: every block against the signed block table). True when the
archive is unsigned (nothing to check against) or everything matches.

members.name: VerificationLevel
members.doc: Resolved `meaf.Verify` for THIS archive (auto resolves by signedness).

members.name: UsesBlockVerification
members.doc:
True when reads of this archive are checked block by block against a
signed v7 block table. Blocks hashed so far, out of the table's rows —
zero right after mount is the point.

members.name: PrefaultPreloadEntries
members.signature: uint64_t PrefaultPreloadEntries(const std::vector<std::string>* openOrder = nullptr) const
members.doc:
Pages every Preload-flagged entry of the mapped archive in with one
sequential walk (the cook lays the global segment out contiguously),
so the first frame's assets don't fault in one page at a time mid-load.
No-op when the archive isn't memory-mapped. Returns bytes touched.
With `openOrder` (the keys a recorded session opened, first open first)
those entries are paged in first, in that order, and the Preload walk
skips them.

members.name: PrefaultPreloadEntriesAsync
members.doc:
The same walk on a thread of its own, so mounting returns at once and
the first loads overlap the paging instead of waiting behind it, driven
by the open order the archive carries (MEAF_OPEN_ORDER_KEY) when it has
one. The walk yields to Unload. GetPrefaultedBytes reads what it touched
once it has finished (0 until then); IsPrefaultRunning says whether it
has; GetPrefaultOrderedEntries how many entries the order paged in.

members.doc: The open order packed into the archive, empty when it carries none.

types.name: FMeafCrypto
types.doc:
Crypto primitives shared by the MEAF packer (MeafBuilder) and the
runtime reader — one implementation so nonce derivation can never
drift between the two. Backed by Monocypher (XChaCha20, BLAKE2b,
EdDSA); the SDK types stay inside the cpp.

members.doc:
XChaCha20 in place. startByte MUST be a multiple of 64 (the cipher
block) — callers align their reads and slice afterwards, which is
what makes partial reads of encrypted entries seekable.

members.name: DeriveTocNonce

members.doc:
Deterministic nonces: derived from content so a repack with
identical content produces identical bytes (patch-friendly), and
any content change changes the nonce.

members.signature: static void TocSalt(const uint8_t key[32], const void* toc, size_t size, uint32_t outSalt[2])
members.doc:
v6. The salt is a BLAKE2b of the whole plaintext TOC keyed with the
archive key: still deterministic, so a rebuild is byte-identical, but
no two different TOCs share it, and without the key it says nothing
about the paths inside. The nonce is derived from the salt and size.

the compression settings while identical output still lands on
identical ciphertext. Kept only to open archives already built: the
CRC32 it keys on is forgeable, so two same-size payloads at one path
with colliding CRCs shared a keystream.

(HashStored). Still deterministic, so an unchanged file repacks to

types.name: FMeafKeyRing
types.doc:
Runtime keys for encrypted / signed MEAF archives, registered BEFORE the
first archive mounts. A packaged host registers the keys `mbt package`
embedded in its executable from the project's Config/DefaultCrypto.ini
(FEmbeddedCryptoKeys); keys never live in any staged file, because
everything staged ships inside the package the key is meant to protect.

The keys live in one locked OS page (IPlatformMemory::AllocateSecretPages)
whose range FCrashHandler tells every minidump writer to leave out, and
nothing hands out a copy: an archive keeps only the key id and decrypts
inside WithKey. A key that sat in heap or in a mounted archive was in
every crash dump uploaded to a third party.

members.signature: static bool RegisterEncryptionKey(const uint8_t key[32], uint32_t keyId = 0)
members.doc:

packer (header.reserved[0]); id 0 is the default single-key setup.
False when the key page could not be allocated or is full.

members.signature: template<typename TFn> static bool WithKey(uint32_t keyId, TFn&& fn)
members.doc:
Runs fn(const uint8_t* key) with the key for keyId, the pointer aimed
into the key page, under a shared lock — fn must not keep the pointer
or copy the bytes anywhere that outlives it. False (fn not called)
when no such key is registered.

types.name: FProjectCryptoSettings
types.doc:
A project's content keys — Config/DefaultCrypto.ini, the analogue of UE's
Project Settings > Crypto. The file is committed with the project: every
build, patch and DLC of one game must be made with the same keys, because the
archive nonces are content-derived and a reader only ever has the key its
host embedded. `mbt package` reads it to encrypt and sign the content paks and
every shipped module, and embeds the encryption key and the signing PUBLIC
key into the packaged host executable; the file itself never ships.

Written by the editor's Crypto page and by `mbt crypto generate`; both write
the same text.

The file holds the signing PUBLIC key only. The private key signs the code a
release game loads (modules, trusted mods, live-ops config), so whoever
could read the game's repository could sign a trojan with it: it lives in
the per-user signing key store (SigningKeyStoreDir, one file per public key —
the same place `mbt` uses) or the MOWO_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY secret of a build
machine. A file that still carries it inline (the layout before 2026-10-13)
loads, and Save moves the key to the store.

types.name: FSignedPayload
types.doc:
FSignedPayload — a text document (remote config, a mod manifest) with a
detached EdDSA signature, in one self-describing JSON envelope:

{"format":"mowo-signed-1","signature":"<128 hex>","payload":"<the text>"}

The signature covers a domain tag plus the payload's exact bytes — never a
re-serialization, so whitespace and key order are the signer's and nothing
a parser does can change what was signed. The key is the project's signing
pair (Config/DefaultCrypto.ini), the one its paks and modules are signed
with; the runtime verifies against the public half the host registered.

members.doc:
The callback runs on the thread that finished the read (an IO worker or
the reaper) instead of the completion pool, so it must only hand the
bytes over. For a caller that is itself a completion callback and waits
for its reads: with every completion worker parked in such a wait,
nothing would be left to deliver to them.

members.name: callback
members.doc: (data, success). Runs on a completion-pool thread.

members.name: cancelToken
members.doc:
Set true to drop the request (checked before AND after the read —
a cancelled in-flight read completes but its callback is skipped).

members.name: Initialize
members.signature: void Initialize(uint32_t ioWorkerCount = 4, uint64_t bandwidthLimitBytesPerSec = 0, uint32_t completionWorkerCount = 0)
members.doc:
bandwidthLimitBytesPerSec throttles Low/Background requests only —
Critical/High/Normal always run at full speed. 0 = unlimited.
completionWorkerCount 0 = a quarter of the cores, between 2 and 4.

members.name: SubmitBatch
members.doc:
Queues every request under one lock, so a run of ranges into one file
reaches the scheduler together and coalesces.

members.name: ReadFilesBlocking
members.signature: std::vector<std::vector<uint8_t>> ReadFilesBlocking(const std::vector<std::string>& paths, IOPriority priority)
members.doc:
Reads every path whole through the queue as one batch and waits; an
entry is empty where its read failed. Callable from a completion
callback (the reads deliver on the read threads), never from an IO
worker. Without a running queue it reads through the VFS.

members.name: PendingCount
members.doc: Stats for the debug overlay / profiler.

members.name: ReadsIssued
members.doc:
Reads actually issued, and requests they served: the gap is what
coalescing saved.

members.name: AsyncBackendName
members.doc:
The asynchronous backend in use ("iocp", "io_uring"), or null when every
read is synchronous. Of ReadsIssued, how many went through it, and the
most that were ever in flight together.

members.name: AsyncDecodedReads
members.doc:
Of AsyncReadsIssued, the whole-entry reads whose stored bytes the
completion pool decoded (encrypted, compressed or block-verified).

members.name: AsyncBytesRead
members.doc:
Bytes the async backend read (stored bytes for a decoded entry). The
synchronous path's bytes are the VFS's StorageBytesRead.

members.name: SetAsyncBackendEnabled
members.doc:
Off forces every read down the synchronous path — for A/B measurement
and for tests. Takes effect from the next Initialize.

types.name: VFS
types.doc:
Mount points, LRU cache, async I/O. Mounting a file system at a virtual path
makes its files reachable under that prefix:
Mount("Content", new NativeFileSystem("C:/Game/Content"))
Open("Content/Textures/player.png") -> C:/Game/Content/Textures/player.png

members.name: TryGet
members.doc:
Null-safe variant for code that may run before the engine (or a
test) constructs the instance.

members.name: Mount
members.signature: void Mount(const std::string& mountPoint, Ref<IFileSystem> fileSystem, int priority = 0)
members.doc:
Higher priority mounts are checked first, which is how overlays win
over the archive they shadow.

members.name: Unmount
members.doc: Drop EVERY file system at this mount point.

members.name: Unmount
members.signature: void Unmount(const std::string& mountPoint, const Ref<IFileSystem>& fileSystem)
members.doc:
Drop one file system from a shared mount point — "Content" carries
both the engine archive and the open project's loose files, and a
project close must not take the engine's with it.

members.name: MountEmbeddedContent
members.doc:
Mounts one embedded content set at FEmbeddedContentRegistry::kMountPriority.
Initialize mounts every registered set; FEmbeddedContentRegistry::Register
calls this for a set that arrives once the VFS is up. A set already
mounted is not mounted twice.

members.name: RemoveNativeRootFallback
members.doc:
Initialize mounts the working directory at the root as the lowest
priority fallback, so any relative key no archive holds is read loose
off the disk. A shipped game must read its content only from the signed
paks: a loose file beside the package would otherwise shadow nothing yet
still load, unsigned and uncompressed, for every key the cook missed.
Absolute paths (saves, the per-user config) keep their passthrough.

members.name: DumpMounts
members.doc:
Logs the mount table and cache occupancy — `vfs.DumpMounts` at the
console; `vfs.LogMisses 1` additionally logs every failed Open with
the mounts that were tried.

members.name: Open
members.signature: Scope<IFile> Open(const std::string& path, FileMode mode = FileMode::Read)

members.name: ListDirectory
members.doc:
The union of every matching mount's listing, one entry per name with
the highest-priority mount's winning, sorted by name. A single mount's
view was wrong for anything layered — engine locales plus project
locales under one prefix, a DLC's files next to the base archive's.

members.name: TryReadFile
members.signature: bool TryReadFile(const std::string& path, std::vector<uint8_t>& outData)
members.doc:
False when the file cannot be opened; an existing empty file fills
outData with nothing and returns true. ReadFile/ReadTextFile cannot
tell those two apart.

members.name: ReadFileShared
members.doc:
Zero-copy variant — a cache hit shares the cached buffer instead
of copying the whole file. Returns nullptr only when the file can't
be opened; an existing empty file yields an empty (cached) buffer, so
it is not re-read from disk on every call. Prefer on hot paths that
only need to LOOK at the bytes.

members.name: ReadFileRange
members.signature: size_t ReadFileRange(const std::string& path, uint64_t offset, size_t size, void* outBuffer)
members.doc:
Partial read — the bytes at [offset, offset+size) without pulling the
whole file into memory. A native file seeks; a MEAF entry that was
cooked block-compressed (the Streamable hint) decompresses only the
blocks the range touches, and one that was not still answers correctly
by inflating the entry. Returns the byte count actually read.

Deliberately NOT cached: the callers are streamers pulling large spans
they immediately hand to the GPU, and putting those through the LRU
would evict everything else to hold bytes nobody reads twice. An
archive entry's open handle IS kept between calls (a small per-path
table), so a sequence of ranges over one entry reuses the MEAF block
cache instead of reopening and re-decompressing the same block every
call; a native file reopens (IFile::ShouldKeepOpenForRanges).

members.name: GetFileSize
members.doc:
Size in bytes through the same kept handle ReadFileRange uses, so a
streamer asking "how big, then give me [a, b)" opens once. -1 when
the file cannot be opened.

members.name: WriteFile
members.signature: bool WriteFile(const std::string& path, const void* data, size_t size)

members.name: WriteTextFile
members.signature: bool WriteTextFile(const std::string& path, const std::string& text)

members.name: ReadFileAsync
members.doc:
Whole-file reads on the compute JobSystem. Streaming and asset loads
go through StreamingIOQueue instead (priorities, cancellation, a
bandwidth budget, dedicated IO workers); these are kept for one-off
callers with no such needs.

members.name: ReadFileAsync
members.signature: void ReadFileAsync(const std::string& path, AsyncReadCallback callback)

members.name: ResolvePhysical
members.signature: bool ResolvePhysical(const std::string& path, FPhysicalLocation& out) const
members.doc:
Where `path`'s bytes sit on disk, resolved the way Open resolves it: the
first mount holding the file answers, and false when that mount cannot
name a plain slice of a native file (a compressed or encrypted archive
entry) — a lower mount is never consulted behind it.

members.name: ResolvePhysicalStored
members.signature: bool ResolvePhysicalStored(const std::string& path, FPhysicalLocation& out) const
members.doc:
The same lookup through IFileSystem::ResolvePhysicalStored: an encrypted,
compressed or block-verified archive entry also resolves, carrying the
decoder an async reader runs on the bytes it read.

members.name: MountGeneration
members.doc:
Moves on every Mount / Unmount, so a holder of a physical location can
tell the mount table it was resolved against is gone.

members.name: StorageReads
members.doc:
Reads the VFS served from storage — read-cache misses and range reads,
the IO queue's synchronous path included — and the bytes they returned,
since start. The async backend's reads never pass here; with the queue's
AsyncBytesRead they are a level load's whole IO.

members.name: SetOpenOrderRecording
members.doc:
Open-order recording (`--record-open-order`): the first time a play
session asks for each relative key — an open, a whole read, a range
read or the streaming queue resolving it — the key is appended. A
package lays its paks out in that order (Config/OpenOrder.txt, `mbt
package --promote-open-order`), so a level load reads forward through
the archive instead of hopping across it. Native absolute paths (saves,
per-user config) are not content and are never recorded.

members.name: WriteOpenOrder
members.doc: One key per line, first open first; false when the file cannot be written.

members.name: ResolveNativePath
members.doc:
Resolve VFS path to an absolute native filesystem path (skips pak mounts).
Returns empty string if the file doesn't exist on any native mount.

members.name: JoinPath
members.signature: static std::string JoinPath(const std::string& a, const std::string& b)

types.name: VFS::FMountInfo
types.doc: The mount table in resolution order (first entry answers first).

The content size a frame declares, or -1 when it declares none or the
